# Independent Iceberg deletion-vector fixture

`iceberg-1.10.0-all-containers.dv` is the unmodified 94-byte golden deletion
vector produced by Apache Iceberg Java 1.10.0. Source revision:
`2114bf631e49af532d66e2ce148ee49dd1dd1f1f` (`apache-iceberg-1.10.0`).

- [Original binary](https://github.com/apache/iceberg/blob/2114bf631e49af532d66e2ce148ee49dd1dd1f1f/core/src/test/resources/org/apache/iceberg/deletes/all-container-types-position-index.bin)
- [Producer and golden-byte assertions](https://github.com/apache/iceberg/blob/2114bf631e49af532d66e2ce148ee49dd1dd1f1f/core/src/test/java/org/apache/iceberg/deletes/TestBitmapPositionDeleteIndex.java)
- [Java DV serializer](https://github.com/apache/iceberg/blob/2114bf631e49af532d66e2ce148ee49dd1dd1f1f/core/src/main/java/org/apache/iceberg/deletes/BitmapPositionDeleteIndex.java)
- [Pinned Puffin specification](https://github.com/apache/iceberg/blob/2114bf631e49af532d66e2ce148ee49dd1dd1f1f/format/puffin-spec.md)

The original file is Copyright the Apache Software Foundation and licensed
under the Apache License 2.0, included in the repository's [LICENSE](../../../../../LICENSE).
The upstream attribution notice is retained in [NOTICE](NOTICE).
No upstream source code was copied into the codec or generation script.

SHA-256 of the original binary:
`98f569f1e0dfe39d38b83c8b3c852d3ba1e7fd8179bb4da19dc94f5318ec70ae`.

`testAllContainerTypesIndexSerialization` writes six logical containers,
including sparse arrays and runs. The producer applies run compression before
serialization. Thus the initially dense contiguous containers also become
runs on disk. The bitmap contains 132561 positions across keys 0 and 1,
including positions above u32::MAX. The Rust suite independently adds a dense
alternating-values case that retains a bitset container.

`iceberg-1.10.0-all-containers.puffin` wraps these exact bytes in an uncompressed
Puffin container; only the wrapper was generated by Bundlebase's Python script.
It has standard metadata and no Bundlebase block identity properties, so the
codec test verifies standard interoperability independently of the core adapter.
The Rust test checks every decoded position against the upstream producer's
input ranges, and checks that our writer reproduces the Java producer's exact
DV payload bytes, rather than merely round-tripping through our own writer.

To reproduce both checked-in files, run from the repository root:

```sh
python3 rust/bundlebase-data/tests/fixtures/puffin/generate.py
```

The script downloads the pinned binary, verifies its SHA-256, DV magic, length
and CRC-32 using Python's independent `zlib` implementation, then writes the
wrapper. Running the Rust tests requires no network or Python dependencies.
To regenerate the original golden DV with its producer, check out the pinned
Apache Iceberg revision and run `TestBitmapPositionDeleteIndex`'s
`testAllContainerTypesIndexSerialization`; its `validate` method requires the
Java-generated bytes to match this original binary exactly.
